name: Prince
hook: A Minneapolis musician who played almost every instrument on his first five albums, built the Minneapolis sound from funk, rock and synthesizers, and changed his name to a symbol to fight his record label.
blurb: Prince Rogers Nelson was born in Minneapolis on 7 June 1958 and wrote his first song on his father's piano at seven. Warner Bros. signed him in 1977, at 18, and gave him creative control over three albums and let him keep his publishing, both of which almost never happened for a new artist. He played nearly every instrument on his first five albums himself: guitar, bass, keyboards, synthesizers and drums. 'Dirty Mind' (1980), 'Controversy' (1981) and '1999' (1982) defined what became called the Minneapolis sound: funk rhythm, rock guitar, and synthesizers where the horns would have been. In 1984, with 'Purple Rain' and 'When Doves Cry', he became the first singer to have the number one film, album and single in America at the same time. Wikipedia lists his influences as including James Brown, George Clinton, Joni Mitchell, Jimi Hendrix, Sly Stone, Little Richard, Curtis Mayfield and Stevie Wonder, and records Miles Davis describing him as a blend of James Brown, Hendrix, Marvin Gaye, Sly Stone and Little Richard. In 1993, in a fight with Warner Bros. over how often his music could be released, he changed his name to a symbol that could not be pronounced. He became a Jehovah's Witness in 2001 through Larry Graham, Sly and the Family Stone's bassist. He died at Paisley Park, his studio complex in Chanhassen, Minnesota, on 21 April 2016, of an accidental overdose of fentanyl, a powerful painkiller.
